subject: literature
passage: When Hira started the ninth grade in Karachi, she inherited her sister Mahnoor's old textbooks, which had been kept, as everything of Mahnoor's was kept, because Mahnoor had been the best student the school had seen in years. Hira expected the margins to be full of help. They were full, but not of help: beside the chemistry equations were question marks, beside a poem the words "I don't get this at all," and on the inside cover a list of dates on which Mahnoor had promised herself to start studying. Hira read every page that evening, long past the point where it helped with her homework. The sister she had always measured herself against had, it turned out, been measuring too, and had been just as uncertain of the result.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Hira is disappointed to find that her sister's notes offer no practical help with her schoolwork.
choices.B: Hira resolves to study harder so that she can match her sister's achievements.
choices.C: Reading Mahnoor's notes, Hira discovers that the sister she had idealized had shared her own doubts.
choices.D: Hira realizes that Mahnoor's reputation as an outstanding student was undeserved.

explanation.why: Hira expects help from the notes of a sister who was "the best student the school had seen in years," but finds question marks, confessions of confusion, and broken promises to start studying. The last sentence states what she learns: the sister she "measured herself against" had been "measuring too" and was "just as uncertain." The main idea is this discovery, not the lack of help.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The notes' uselessness for homework is only the starting point; Hira keeps reading "long past the point where it was useful," because the text is about what she learns about her sister.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text does not describe any decision about Hira's own studying.
explanation.C: Correct. This captures the discovery that the idealized sister had been just as uncertain as Hira.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never questions Mahnoor's achievements; it shows that she had doubts despite them.
